findings.text: the re-ask is paced by the fixed MOVE_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS only, so a checkout that stays dirty pays the full trust test -- which loads every module in the package, as the comment at :128-136 states -- once per minute for as long as it stays dirty, with no backoff and no cap; the repository's owner of retry pacing for exactly this probe is reckon/crew/follower_reload.py:174-195, which doubles FOLLOWER_RELOAD_PROBE_RETRY_INITIAL_SECONDS and jitters it, and following it here would keep the re-ask that this repair correctly restores while bounding its cost on a tree that is dirty for hours. Restoring the earlier fixed-interval behaviour is defensible as the prior reviewed shape, so this does not hold the node.

justifications.durability: tests/test_the_fleet_supervisor_runs_current_code.py:294-323 reddens under the restored per-stamp exclusion because wait_for(run.replacements) never resolves, confirmed by logs/negative-control.log at 1 failed 4 passed, and the arm's later assertions compare the loop's recorded {'running': 'stamp-a', 'disk': 'stamp-b'} against literals the code must derive from its recorded stamp rather than from the test's call, so a regression that passes the current stamp as running would fail them.

justifications.fit: the change follows the module's constant-and-comment idiom at fleet_supervisor.py:128-136 and :2149-2168, and adds no name that carries a plan, sprint or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:2159-2179 now asks the moved_checkout verdict again after each interval while the stamps still differ, so a stamp refused once is adopted when its tree becomes loadable, which is the outage the section describes (a supervisor held on an image older than its checkout until the next commit).
